page: Microsoft Azure E64-16ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. Configured as a constrained-core variant within the Eadsv7 series, it provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance integrates 512 GB of system memory, yielding an expansive 32 GB of RAM per vCPU, along with 3,780 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark evaluations reflect exceptional single-threaded compute efficiency alongside strong memory performance. In single-core stress-ng tests, the instance ranks in the top tier, matching high single-thread throughput observed in gzip compression (41.33 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (18.26 GB/sec). Memory subsystem benchmarks show a strong PassMark memory rating of 2,845.34. Multi-core compute benchmarks, including multi-threaded stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests, register in the middle tier, directly reflecting the 16-vCPU allocation on the underlying 64-vCPU hardware footprint.

The constrained CPU allocation offers distinct cost efficiency advantages for software licensing models priced on a per-core basis, allowing deployments to access substantial memory arrays and local NVMe storage without paying for unneeded vCPUs. Tradeoffs include modest uncached large-block write bandwidth (34.13 GB/sec) and limited throughput on high-parameter computational models, illustrated by lower processing rates on 70B parameter LLM workloads. The configuration does not include discrete GPU acceleration or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Microsoft Azure E64-16ads_v7 is primarily engineered for memory-intensive workloads that require substantial working sets and low per-core licensing footprints. Suitable applications include large-scale relational database engines, in-memory caches, enterprise ERP deployments, heavy data analytics, and intermediate caching layers requiring fast local NVMe storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E64-16ads_v7 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. As a constrained-core configuration, it provides 16 dedicated vCPUs on 8 physical cores paired with 512 GB of RAM, offering a high ratio of 32 GB per vCPU. The hardware setup includes 3,780 GB of direct NVMe SSD storage, while discrete GPU acceleration is absent. Benchmark results highlight top-tier single-core performance and strong memory throughput, complemented by high-speed single-threaded compression capabilities. Multi-core performance remains moderate due to the 16-thread cap, making this instance economically efficient for applications constrained by per-core software licensing costs. This server is ideal for in-memory databases, large caching layers, data analytics pipelines, and memory-heavy enterprise database workloads.
